evals.prompt: Hunt through this repo for TODOs that you could actually just go fix. Show me a candidate list with a one-line fix plan and expected diff size for each. Don't create any worktrees or modify anything yet; I just want to see the list first. The repo is at <REPO>.
evals.expected_output: A candidate table listing every actionable, test-verifiable TODO (no artificial cap), each with file:line, TODO text, fix plan, and diff-size estimate — and nothing else: no exclusion lists or justifications, and no advance catalog of choices the user would veto. Blocked TODOs (unmet preconditions) simply do not appear. No candidates from define/spec/, define/proposals/, drafts/, or TODO.md. Repo left completely unmodified.
expectations: No candidate comes from define/spec/, define/proposals/, drafts/, or TODO.md
TODOs whose stated precondition is unmet (e.g. the protocompile EDITION_2024 test skip, deleting action_call_graph.py while destructors are unimplemented) do not appear as candidates

Actionable TODOs are not excluded for involving design choices, user-facing behavior changes, efficiency work, or large mechanical diffs — for example, both the automated_requirements_nested_action_test.py file split and the dead operation_graph field removal appear as candidates
Every candidate lists file:line, a one-line fix plan, and an expected diff size
The repo is left completely unmodified: clean git status, no new branches, no worktrees, no define2-todos directory
The report contains only the candidate list — nothing about TODOs not being proposed (no exclusion lists, categories, or justifications) and no advance catalog of choices the user would be vetoing

evals.prompt: I have a feeling there was a TODO fix from last week that I never got around to reviewing. Can you check what's pending in the repo at <REPO> and tell me how to look at it?
evals.expected_output: Discovers the todo/rename-parse-fqun worktree via git, reports it as ready for review (staged uncommitted changes, no commits of its own), gives the exact review command, and touches nothing.
expectations: The report identifies the pending fix in the todo/rename-parse-fqun worktree
The report accurately describes its state: staged, uncommitted changes awaiting the user's review
The report gives a command that actually shows the pending diff (e.g. git -C <worktree> diff --cached)
The seeded state is untouched: the worktree still exists with the identical staged diff, no new commits anywhere, main checkout clean
No new hunt or fix work was started uninvited (no new branches or worktrees)

evals.prompt: There's a TODO in define/compiler/name_parser.py about renaming _parse_fqun that looks trivially fixable. Prepare a fix for it in a git worktree so I can review it before anything lands — consider the candidate pre-approved, no need to check with me on the plan. Stop when it's ready for my review. The repo is at <REPO>.
evals.expected_output: A todo/<slug> branch with a sibling worktree containing the rename as staged, uncommitted changes with the TODO comment removed. Branch has no commits of its own; nothing committed or pushed; full Bazel suite run in the worktree; report says how to review.
expectations: The fix exists as staged, uncommitted changes in a dedicated git worktree on a todo/* branch — not in the main checkout
The todo/* branch has no commits of its own (its tip equals main)
The staged diff removes the TODO comment and renames _parse_fqun at both use sites, and changes nothing else
Nothing was committed or pushed: origin/main still points at the seeded commit and the main checkout is clean
The full Bazel test suite (bazelisk test //...) was run against the fixed tree and passed, per the run's report
The final report tells the user exactly how to review the staged diff
